title: A 12-Year-Old Gives Old Stuffed Animals a Second Life — and Comfort to Kids in Need
summary:
A soft toy can mean a lot to a child going through a hard time. That is why American Red Cross volunteers always keep stuffed animals on hand for children affected by disasters. Earlier this year, though, the Red Cross in North Carolina ran low. As it responded to more home fires, its supply of the comfort items was running short.

Disaster Program Specialist Jon McCollum reached out to the community for help. His request caught the attention of 12-year-old Sadie Hutson. Moved by the stories of displaced families, she and her mother began buying discarded stuffed animals from local thrift stores. Sadie then restored each toy, carefully washing it, mending torn seams and even replacing missing stuffing.

By early summer, she had restored and donated 114 bears, rabbits, puppies and other stuffed toys to the Red Cross. That is a mountain of second chances, one soft friend at a time. Her efforts were recognised in September 2026, when McCollum and fellow volunteers honoured Sadie with a Young Humanitarian Award.

Sadie was excited to receive the award, but she said that was not why she started the project. 'Hearing the stories was a little heartbreaking,' Sadie said. 'That's why I did it.' She hopes her story will inspire other young people to help in their own communities. Meanwhile, she plans to keep donating restored stuffed animals, so children facing difficult times have something soft to hold on to.

One washed bear, one mended seam, one fresh handful of stuffing — small repairs, but each one carries a little comfort to a child who needs it.
why_it_matters: Sadie's project shows that one young person can make a real difference for children going through frightening times. It also shows how small, patient work, one washed bear at a time, can add up to something big.

background_read: The American Red Cross is a charity that helps people after disasters such as fires and floods, giving them shelter, food and comfort.
Volunteers often hand out soft toys to children because something familiar to hold can help a child feel calmer in a frightening time.
Thrift stores sell second-hand goods at low prices, so they are a good place to find old toys that can be cleaned and fixed.
When families lose their homes, they may have to leave quickly with very little, which is why donations of comfort items matter.
